content: 1. Clark H, Coll-Seck AM, Banerjee A, Peterson S, Dalglish SL, Ameratunga S, and colleagues authored a report titled A Future for the World’s Children? This was a collaborative effort by the WHO, UNICEF, and The Lancet Commission, published in The Lancet in 2020 (Volume 395, Pages 605–658). The report discusses the future health and well-being of children globally. 2. Boyland E conducted a rapid scoping review on food marketing targeted at children and the effectiveness of restrictive policies. This unpublished report was prepared for the World Health Organization in Geneva in 2018. 3. A WHO report titled Tackling Food Marketing to Children in a Digital World explores transdisciplinary perspectives, including children’s rights, evidence of marketing impacts, methodological challenges, regulatory options, and policy implications for the WHO European Region. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 4. WHO guidelines on policies to protect children from the harmful effects of food marketing provide a framework for implementing recommendations on marketing foods and non-alcoholic beverages to children. This document was accessed on May 8, 2023. 5. Kelly B, King ML, Chapman K, Boyland E, Bauman AE, and Baur LA published a study in American Journal of Public Health (2015; Volume 105, Pages e86–e95) that outlines a hierarchy of the effects of unhealthy food promotion. The study identifies methodological approaches and knowledge gaps in this area. 6. The United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child issued General Comment No. 15 (2013) on the right of children to enjoy the highest attainable standard of health, as outlined in Article 24 of the Convention on the Rights of the Child. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 7. WHO has developed a comprehensive implementation plan on maternal, infant, and young child nutrition, which was accessed on May 9, 2023. 8. The Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Noncommunicable Diseases (2013–2020) outlines strategies to reduce the global burden of noncommunicable diseases. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 9. The WHO Commission on Ending Childhood Obesity released a report detailing strategies to combat childhood obesity. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 10. The Global Nutrition Policy Review (2016–2017) evaluates country progress in creating enabling policy environments to promote healthy diets and nutrition. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 11. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2nd Edition) provides detailed guidance on developing evidence-based health guidelines. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 12. WHO and UNICEF are collaborating on a forthcoming report titled Taking Action to Protect Children from the Harmful Impact of Food Marketing: A Child Rights-Based Approach. 13. WHO is preparing forthcoming guidelines on nutrition labeling policies, fiscal policies to promote healthy diets, and school food and nutrition policies. 14. WHO guidelines on sodium intake for adults and children, as well as sugar intake, provide evidence-based recommendations to reduce the risk of diet-related diseases. These documents were accessed on May 9, 2023. 15. The Thirteenth General Programme of Work (2019–2023) outlines WHO’s strategic priorities to promote health, ensure global safety, and serve vulnerable populations. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 16. WHO’s adolescent health initiatives focus on improving the health and well-being of adolescents worldwide. This information was accessed on May 9, 2023. 17. Balshem H, Helfand M, Schunemann HJ, Oxman AD, Kunz R, Brozek J, and colleagues published GRADE guidelines in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology (2011; Volume 64, Pages 401–406) to rate the quality of evidence in health research. 18. Dhar T and Baylis K examined the impact of banning fast-food advertising targeting children in Quebec, publishing their findings in Journal of Marketing Research (2011; Volume 48, Pages 799–813). 19. WHO’s European Region report evaluates the implementation of recommendations on marketing foods and beverages to children, highlighting progress, challenges, and next steps. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 20. WHO and UNESCO are developing global standards and indicators to make every school a health-promoting school. This initiative aims to integrate health into the education system. 21. Phulkerd S, Lawrence M, Vandevijvere S, Sacks G, Worsley A, and Tangcharoensathien V reviewed methods to assess government policies for creating healthy food environments. Their findings were published in Implementation Science (2016; Volume 11, Article 15). 22. Lakerveld J, Woods C, Hebestreit A, Brenner H, Flechtner-Mors M, Harrington JM, and colleagues advanced the evidence base for public policies affecting dietary behavior, physical activity, and sedentary behavior in Europe. Their work was published in Food Policy (2020; Volume 96, Article 101873). 23. WHO’s monitoring protocols and templates for marketing unhealthy products to children and adolescents provide tools for assessing digital marketing practices. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 24. Kelly B, King L, Baur L, Rayner M, Lobstein T, Monteiro C, and colleagues published a study in Obesity Reviews (2013; Volume 14, Pages 59–69) on monitoring food and beverage promotions targeting children. 25. Peters D, Tran N, Adam T, and the Alliance for Health Policy and Systems Research at WHO authored a practical guide on implementation research in health. This document was accessed on May 9, 2023. 26. Ngqangashe Y, Friel S, and Schram A analyzed regulatory governance conditions that support effective food policies for population nutrition. Their findings were published in Public Health Nutrition (2021). 27. WHO’s forthcoming guidelines on school health services aim to improve the delivery of health services in educational settings. 28. WHO and UNICEF are preparing a policy brief on protecting children from the harmful impact of food marketing. 29. WHO’s regional action framework for the Western Pacific focuses on protecting children from harmful food marketing practices. 30. The WHO Nutrition Guidance Expert Advisory Group (NUGAG) Subgroup on Policy Actions includes experts from various countries and disciplines, contributing to the development of global nutrition policies.
